mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-inflationary period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS < previous month and INDPRO > previous month) creates a labor market softening that precedes a 20-day S&P 500 bearish reversal.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND INDPRO > previous month
regime_hint: labor market transition from expansion to moderation
failure_condition: Over 10 testing windows, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative relative to the 5-day pre-signal baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 10% month-over-month signals accelerating consumer confidence and supports a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Across 50 backtests, the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness that precedes a 20-day S&P 500 decline.
failure_condition: No significant 20-day downward move in SPX during the three-month contraction window (maximum drawdown < 2%).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +4% in a month following a negative FEDFUNDS surprise, it signals aggressive price inflation that depresses 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In 10 such inflation events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months without a corresponding rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market that precedes a 20-day S&P 500 rally.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months AND PAYEMS < previous month
failure_condition: Over 15 backtests, the 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 5-day pre-signal baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent divergence between S&P 500 1-month momentum (log returns > 0) and the 5-day moving average of FEDFUNDS creates a contrarian signal that predicts a positive 20-day forward return when the divergence lasts more than 3 months.
candidate_trigger: SPX 1-mo momentum > 0 AND FEDFUNDS 5-mo MA < SPX 1-mo momentum for > 3 months
failure_condition: Across 40 tests, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive when the divergence condition is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL 12-mo change < -2%) and persistent rate hikes (FEDFUNDS 12-mo change > +0.5%), the S&P 500 exhibits a 60-day bullish bias as investors anticipate a normalization period.
failure_condition: In 20 historical episodes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 30-day pre-deflation baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
